rows.title: Hook 01
rows.prompt:
Animate the approved opening into one continuous 3-second portrait clip. Keep the same influencer, black top, pink keyboard, curtains and magenta-lit shelves.

0.00–1.76s: Hold the wide-eyed, open-mouth stare upward toward screen-right with hands low at the desk. Allow the early natural blink, without smiling or lifting a hand to the mouth yet.
1.76–2.09s: Bring the gaze nearer the lens and lift the screen-right hand to cover the mouth. The other hand leaves the keyboard and reaches directly toward the recording phone, near the lens.
2.09–2.77s: Keep the same hand covering the mouth and eyes wide. The reaching hand takes hold of the recording phone outside its own view and begins lifting it from the desk-supported position. The viewpoint moves closer and tilts with brief irregular handheld shake and motion softness. This is physical camera handling, not a smooth digital zoom. Keep holding the phone; do not withdraw that hand back to the keyboard.
2.77–3.00s: Continue lifting and tilting the handheld phone toward the face, retaining the small uneven shake. End in a very tight off-center crop with part of the face outside the screen-right edge, while the same hand stays over the mouth. Do not settle back into a centered desk shot before the final frame or introduce a second visible phone.

Preserve identity, outfit, scene and hand contact. Keep the camera low and still during the opening hold; the handheld movement begins only after the reaching gesture. No captions, scene cuts, speech or music.

rows.title: Hook 99

sourceIntervals.action: Hold the open-mouth surprised look with the already raised hand beside the cheek. Bring the screen-left gaze toward the lens without covering the mouth yet.
Move that same raised hand across the mouth, maintaining a surprised gaze.
Hold the hand against the mouth continuously. Glance briefly screen-left then back toward the lens; keep the eyes open and alert.

Keep the mouth covered while the handheld selfie camera moves closer and its viewpoint tilts upward. The face grows larger and ceiling becomes prominent. Do not substitute only a body lean for camera movement.
Briefly close the eyes while the same hand still covers the mouth; retain the closer crop.
Reopen the eyes and lower that same hand away from the mouth as the mouth opens again.
Keep the open-mouth reaction toward the lens through the final frame in the closer selfie view; no new gesture or scene transition.

Blink or briefly close the eyes and turn the head slightly screen-left, drawing the tongue back and pursing the lips. Keep the same bottle grip.
Turn toward the lens and settle briefly into a small closed-lip smile; hand and upright bottle stay near the chin and chest.

Continue the mouth/hand action while the camera tilts upward toward the wall and ceiling. Let the performer move into the lower-left of the picture, with part of the head cut by the bottom edge in the final view. Do not recenter the person or add a bottle-to-mouth sip.
